OUR FAMILY
Raised Right

We started Marble Creek Farms with one goal - to raise animals the right way and provide food we'd proudly serve to our own family. We don't just raise kids and animals. Our legacy is built in the spirit of our kids and within what we provide to our soils. That is not something we take lightly, and we strive to be good stewards of what blessings we've been given.

YOUR BEEF
Our Promise

At Marble Creek Farms, we believe food should come from a source you can verify and with a story you can trust. We feed our family the same products we sell to yours.

No growth hormones
No antibiotics
No herbicides or pesticides
No animal by-products
Cattle raised on pasture

WHAT WE OFFER

Tallow Products

Why Regenerative Farming?

We don't just raise animals - we build soil, restore ecosystems, and improve the land with every pasture rotation. Moving the cattle herd multiple times each week, pulling our laying hen flock and broiler chickens behind the cattle, and letting the grass and soil rest for 30-45 days after each pass, gives the soil time to heal and grass plenty of time to recover.

ABOUT US
Built From the Ground Up - One Animal, One Acre at a Time

Blake and Kayla Miller are a first generation farm family starting from the ground up. Neither grew up in a farm family, in fact, both grew up outside major metro areas - Houston, TX and Atlanta, GA. With a background in wealth management and business strategy, Blake always had a curiosity of different ways to be an entrepreneur and he enjoys the thrill of building a business from scratch. When 2020 hit and grocery store shelves went empty, Blake saw that as the perfect entry point to start building a farm and controlling the supply chain to secure his family's food. Over the course of the next two years, Blake spent time volunteering on the weekends at farms nearby, soaking up the knowledge and experience of local farmers just hoping to have his own farm and cattle operation one day. As the perfect amount of persistency and luck would have it, Blake and Kayla got their first farm in 2023 just outside of Gainesville, GA. It was a diamond in the rough, an old farm needing a lot of TLC that had been used to cut hay for the prior 10 years. It was the perfect project for Blake and Kayla to bring back to life and begin their new journey into land and animal stewardship. The Millers now have multiple properties in Gainesville and Jasper where they raise beef cattle and pastured chicken and eggs.

Raising The Next Generation

As Blake and Kayla started their journey into agriculture, they were 3 months into having a brand new baby boy. Although timing was not ideal to begin two major life changes at once, both were incredible blessings that have been able to flourish together since then. The Millers now have two young boys, with the oldest taking advantage of every opportunity to be out at the farm helping any way he can. The Millers strive to create an environment on the farm with their family that will last for generations.

Why Cattle Genetics Mattered Early

If the ultimate goal of starting a farm was to raise premium beef, Blake and Kayla knew that all had to start with the right genetics. With Blake's background in finance and having a passion for data, the genetic and biological data was a new challenge that was gladly accepted. The first cow that Blake and Kayla purchased ended up being a home run, and she has now generated multiple daughters that are all being built around for the herd retention program.

KNOWING YOUR FARMER, KNOWING YOUR FOOD
If Our Animals Can't Thrive On Grass, They Don't Belong Here

We are all becoming more and more aware of what is in our food, how it is made, and the processes that are being used to grow, raise, ship, and deliver it to us. It's no secret that the industrial agriculture model is broken and disruption is required to change our current systems for the better. 

Raising two young boys, we wanted to raise animals in a regenerative agriculture system without the use of antibiotics, vaccines, growth hormones, pesticides, herbicides, and the like. All of that may ultimately be fine, but we don't want to eat it and we don't want our kids to eat it.

The food that is grown on our farms is the same food we feed our family, and we want to grow enough so we can feed yours too. The Millers at Marble Creek Farms would love to be one of your local farmers.

Join Our Community

Become a member of our Marble Creek Farms community and receive regular updates about our products and availability. We offer everything from bulk beef, beef boxes, individual cuts, whole chickens, and eggs by the dozen. Stay tuned for a brand new line of tallow cosmetics made with all natural ingredients for men, women, and babies.

Our Farming Philosophy

 To bring fresh, straight from the farm, pasture-raised and grass-fed, high quality meats to our community, so they can enjoy well-marbled, flavorful, and health-conscious proteins that their friends and family will be talking about for years to come! 

LEARN OUR FARMING PRACTICES
REGENERATIVE AGRICULTURE IN ACTION
Rotational Grazing

Cattle have high impacts to the soils and plant life in an area, which allows opportunity for trampling forage and consuming forage. When rotated right, there is a perfect blend of both and this allows plant regrowth to occur in as little as 21 days. 

Chicken Impact After Cattle

Bringing in our laying hens and meat broilers 2-5 days after the cattle have grazed an area allows the chickens to eat the pests, fly larvae, bugs, and parasites which then reduces the nuisance populations as we enter into the warmer months each season. Chickens also help distribute manure patties throughout the pasture allowing for increased natural fertilizer and eliminates the reliance of chemicals on our farm.

Soil Health First

Although we raise animals, the most important resource we produce is grass and edible vegetation for our animals. The only way we can increase our production per acre is if we have great soil health, with optimal nutrient levels, encouraging good bacteria to grow, and increasing the earth worm and dung beetle populations. Soil biology is the first thing we focus on, and it's what has allowed us to graze further and further into winter each year before feeding hay.

Animal Welfare

There are more and more studies that are coming out that show how important animal stress levels are to the quality of beef. The more stressed an animal is, the tougher the meat. When animals are free to roam on pastures, without being confined to penned lots, those animals tend to have increased tenderness within those cuts of beef. When you combine that with high quality genetics, the result is something you'll never experience from a grocery store.

Grass Finished

High in Omega-3 fatty acids, conjugated linoleic acid, and antioxidants, 100% grass fed beef tends to result in a very high nutritional profile and adheres more to the natural diet of cattle. We are currently running multiple on farm tests to compare the genetic results based on multiple different breeds to continually improve our finished on grass genetics. With top genetics, and grass diversity in our pastures, every day our cattle are on pasture they are getting a blend of high protein legumes and nutrient dense forages. Everyone loves a steak, however our grass finished ground beef is one that our customers can't get enough of. 

Grain Finished

Cattle have been finished on grain for decades and it's what every customer of a high quality steakhouse in America expects when they take that first bite. The higher fat content from corn finished beef often results in a much higher marbling profile than grass finished, with a melt-in-your-mouth experience. Our focus is to deliver the highest quality steak eating experience, similar to what you would have at the top steakhouses in the country. Through many trials, we've developed a custom blend feeding program that allows our cattle to finish out within 120-200 days.

BEEF THE WAY IT WAS MEANT TO BE
100% American Beef Raised in North Georgia

Every animal that we raise is born and raised on one of our Georgia farms. The supply chain starts at Marble Creek Farms and ends at Marble Creek Farms. No middle men. No international shipping. No auction-cattle. We control the beginning and the end, which is the only way to 100% trust where that beef comes from (we are working on QR codes and blockchain technology to improve that).

RAISED ON THE FARM
Grass vs Grain-Finished

Everyone has different flavor profiles they like and preferences on how to cook beef. Grass-finished requires a "low and slow" method, whereas grain-finished provides a little more grace when cooking. A reverse-sear on grass-finished steak is Blake's personal favorite.

Breeding Advantage

Utilizing a 3-way cross between Gelbvieh, Angus (Black and Red), and Akaushi (Red Wagyu), this allows the optimal genetic diversity for heterosis. Gelbvieh has growth, Angus has feed efficiency, and Akaushi has marbling excellence.

Flavor + Nutrition

Compared to conventional, industrial beef, local beef raised on pasture tends to result in high quality steaks, roasts, and ground beef products. High in vitamins, minerals, antioxidants, and omega-3's, there is a reason more people are going to local beef suppliers.

Traceability

In today's world, the global economy is fully interconnected and our food supply chain is no different. Much of our beef comes from inside the US, however we import a lot more than most realize. At Marble Creek Farms, all of our beef is born, raised, and finished on our farms.

Cut Options

At Marble Creek Farms, we offer a variety of bulk beef boxes as well as individual cuts. We understand that not everyone has the space for a big freezer, so we've designed subscription boxes to help families get high quality beef right off the farm.

Bulk Buying

Buying in bulk with family or friends is one of the best ways to get high premium beef at an incredible price. Usually for the same price per pound of ground beef at the store, you can get an entire beef in your freezer for around the same price per pound. An incredible value!
